posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Game title:
The 2026 "I Love You!" Banner, Limited Time! Available Until
RPG Maker used:
RPG Maker MV
Did you use any scripts/plugins?:
Not in the Ensh/tified version.
Credits:
Ensh/tified version:
No one.
Version before we sought profits over quality:
ATT_Turan, Mac15001900, SRD, Yami, Yanfly
Character chosen:
I chose all the wonderful SFX and RTP animations.
Link:
The 2026 "I Love You" Banner, Limited Time! Available until by NolanAlighieri
Get the characters you love and make new players feel obligated to buy by rolling in our "I Love You" 2026 Banner!
nolanalighieri.itch.io
Note to judges of the jam:
Please download the "Ensh/tified" version. This version is truly and purely only RTP. No plugins. Do data compression. Raw
profit
badge-seeking over any intent for a quality product.
A statement on plugin usage (this statement is only relevant to the pre-profit-profit seeking version of the game):
Spoiler:
Statement
ATT_Turan: Dev Master Volume Plugin - used to set the starting volume of the game lower.
Mac15001900: Mac High Hz Fix - used to prevent crashes and unnecessary CPU overhead for users of high refresh rate monitors.
SRD:
Camera Core - used because the entire game is built on a single map and I was too lazy to force a bounding box for the camera during character selection.
Fullscreen Option - used because it was quicker to drop it into my plugin folder and enable it to launch the game in full screen, rather than look up and refresh my memory on the script to force full screen.
Yami: Skip Title - used because the title scene is unnecessary for this game.
Yanfly:
Region Restrictions - used because the game is 1 map, so regions were used to create a bounding space in the character selection
Keyboard Config - Used to enable WASD and arrow keys for movement
Message Core - used to enable word wrapping because of the randomly generated text (it was difficult to know how or where the line should break. Word wrapping simplifies that)
As stated, none of these have direct influence on the mechanics or systems of the game.
About the game logic (I recommend only reading it after playing the game)
Spoiler:
RANDOM FACTOR & GOLD COST
Do not play this game to win. That is the satire of the game.
Technically speaking, it is possible to "win" the game, but you would need to have godlike fortune to make it happen.
SELECTING A CHARACTER:
When you define the character you want, the game will make a note of that. This character will be set to a number. If that number of your character is rolled, then the game will roll a second time. If it rolls your character's number on the second roll, then you win the character roll.
CHARACTER STAR RATING
After the character is rolled, you will get a star rating for that character. Stars are awarded with a separate random number roll with depreciating values: 35% chance for 1 star, 25% 2 star, 20% 3 star, 15% 4 star, 5% 5 star.
As the game progresses, these values change. I will explain how later.
MONEY PAY OUT
Each star rating is what determines your rewarded money.
The payout formula is simple: 33 money per each star.
RATE CHANGE OVER TIME
The cost of rolling for a character and the chance of getting higher star value characters changes as the game progresses.
Each cycle from character selection, to character pull, back to character selection increases the game state by 1. This game state value is used as a negative modifier to your random rolls, basically decreasing your luck (though the effect is largely unnoticeable for the first few rounds since we are dealing with roll numbers around 150 - a change of 1 is .5% reduction in luck)
Each new character pull you do will guarantee an increased cost of 2 money per pull.
Star ratings affect cost further. 1 - 3 stars have no effect. 4 stars increases the next round cost by 3, while 5 increases it by 4
Finally, once the game state increases to 7, and again at 16, all cost values are increased by 1 and 2 respectively.
WINNING
:
In order to "Win" the game, you must pull the 5 star version of the character you chose in the character selection screen.
Fun facts with Nolan:
Spoiler:
FUN FACTS INSIDE!
I finally bought MZ, but I still used MV to make this because of it's Linux support. It's nice accessing it's RTP now, though.
This game was built under 24 hours.
Many of the characters are references to friends, regular chatters in my stream, my own game, or users on RMW.
If you see a contraction in the writing missing an apostrophe, that likely means that was one of the randomly generated lines. It could also mean I was hasty when writing the text and forgot it.
This game actually makes sense, unlike my last Jam game.
I was totally fine with not getting the RTP Hero badge, but then I got "Dude, Really!?!"'d and it hurt my feelings. I felt ATT_Bullied and decided to pursue profit growth over an actual product.

posts.author: Lady_JJ
posts.body:
Game title: Everybody Loves Blanchette
RPG Maker used: MZ v 1.9.0
Copyright (c) Gotcha Gotcha Games, Inc.
Yoji Ojima 2020
Did you use any scripts/plugins?: No
Credits: hiddenone for hosting this event
Character chosen: Actor 3-6 (I named her Blanchette, the name of Little Red Riding Hood in the French version) I really like her innocent, youthful look
Link:
Everybody Loves Blanchette
This is a simple fetch it type game with optional puzzles. The game can be played in less than 15 minutes by merely (1) fetching milk and eggs for mom, (2) gathering 5 bunches of mushrooms for the shopkeeper, Andrei, and (3) filling 5 empty vials for the sorcerer, Celeste, then revisiting Granny. However, there is a 4th optional fetching quest and 4 optional puzzles. Solving the 4 optional puzzles allows you to defeat the boss without hiring heroes. That adds another 15-20 minutes to the game.
Thank you to
@hiddenone
and everyone else involved for hosting this game jam.
Note that RPG Maker games, itch.io, and Chrome don't appear to be playing nicely. I can't play any of the itch embedded browser versions In Chrome, whether made by myself or by others. It doesn't appear to be unique to me as other members of my family have visited itch.io using their own computers and own network with the same results. If you get a
Failed to initialize graphics
error with Chrome, please try using another browser such as Edge instead.

Revered through the land for his saintly deeds, Arthur seems like he has it all. One day, however, he summons an angel in hopes of filling a hole in his heart...
